note: Mega Phase D, PR D4: real macOS/Metal backend + launchd service-lifecycle abstraction. D1/D2/D3's own real squash SHAs backfilled here, matching this mega-phase's own convention. All REAL evidence below comes from GitHub Actions' macos-14 hosted runner (the macos-metal-smoke CI job) across several real, iterative runs -- CI run IDs 34000242949 (initial build failure: memfd_create), 34001074361 (build failure: st_mtim), 34001944212 (own CI job bug: test_launchd_unit never built), 34002663786 (full pipeline green except real generation used --ctx auto, which correctly fails closed on macOS), 34003445799 (full pipeline green including real Metal generation with an explicit --ctx).

hardware.label: REAL
hardware.gpu: MTL0 (Apple Paravirtual device), 4778.7 MiB reported total/free
hardware.runner: GitHub Actions macos-14 hosted runner -- real Apple Silicon cloud infrastructure, but this job executes inside a paravirtualized VM, not with direct/bare-metal GPU access (confirmed directly by the device's own self-reported name, not inferred)
hardware.caveat: A materially weaker hardware-scope claim than PR D3's CUDA validation (a real, bare-metal GTX 1650) or the existing Vulkan rows -- real compatibility is genuinely established here, but no performance conclusion should be drawn from this run's own throughput numbers. See docs/macos-metal.md's own 'Hardware scope' section.

build_integration.label: REAL
evidence: Real CMake configure with -DGGML_METAL=ON on macos-14: '-- Metal framework found', successful 'Embedding Metal library' step, 'Built target ggml-metal' -- no extra dependency install needed (Metal/Foundation/MetalKit ship with the OS).

A new, MEMBRANE-level CMakeLists.txt pre-check (GGML_METAL AND NOT APPLE -> FATAL_ERROR) mirrors the existing GGML_VULKAN/GGML_CUDA pattern -- fails clearly before ever descending into third_party/llama.cpp's own ggml-metal/CMakeLists.txt find_library(... REQUIRED) calls.
ggml-metal joined tools/membrane-run/CMakeLists.txt's existing install/RPATH TARGET-guarded foreach loop the same way ggml-cuda/ggml-vulkan already do.

A real, previously-undiscovered cross-platform RPATH bug was found and fixed BEFORE the first real Metal build was even attempted: the existing install-time RPATH used the Linux/ELF-only '$ORIGIN' token unconditionally, which dyld (macOS) does not understand at all. Fixed via a platform-selected token (MEMBRANE_RPATH_ORIGIN_TOKEN: '@loader_path' on Darwin, unchanged '$ORIGIN' elsewhere), computed once and reused everywhere INSTALL_RPATH is set.

Two further real, genuine portability bugs were found and fixed via the real macOS CI build's own compiler errors, in order: (1) memfd_create() (tools/membrane-run/main.cpp) -- a real Linux-only glibc/kernel syscall with no Darwin equivalent, replaced with the portable POSIX tmpfile() (a strict improvement, not a workaround); (2) struct stat's st_mtim field (three independent call sites: server.cpp, model_cmd.cpp, doctor_cmd.cpp) -- POSIX.1-2008 naming, real on Linux/glibc but named st_mtimespec on macOS/BSD, fixed via one new shared, portable membrane_stat_mtime_ns() helper (fs_util.h/.cpp) rather than three independent #ifdef copies.

Zero changes needed anywhere in gpu_policy.c, context_recommender.c, compat_check.c, or the joint planner -- confirmed directly by grep (no hardcoded backend-name string in any of them) and by this PR's own real Metal generation succeeding with zero code changes to any of them, exactly matching PR D3's own CUDA finding.

Full existing CPU/Vulkan/CUDA-relevant local Linux test suite (build-b1) reconfirmed unaffected across every commit on this branch: 89/89 ctest passed each time, including the two new membrane_launchd_unit-related targets.

real_device_enumeration.label: REAL
evidence: `membrane-run --list-devices` (macos-metal-smoke, real CI output): 'MTL0 (Apple Paravirtual device)' (4778.7 MiB total/free) alongside 'BLAS (Accelerate)' and 'CPU (Apple M1 (Virtual))'.

`membrane-run --doctor` (same run): '[OK] GPU backend compiled in', '[OK] GPU device: MTL0 (Apple Paravirtual device)' -- no code change needed to report this; the existing, backend-agnostic diagnostic just worked, same finding as PR D3.

`membrane-run --doctor` also reported '[WARN] host RAM could not be read (non-Linux host, or /proc/meminfo unavailable)' -- a real, honest, pre-existing limitation (host_memory_guard.h's own host-RAM reader is Linux-only), disclosed rather than hidden -- see docs/macos-metal.md's own 'Known limitations'.

real_generation.label: REAL
evidence: Real HTTPS model download from Hugging Face via the existing D1/D2 product path: `membrane model install smollm2:135m --quant q4_k_m` -- real size validation and real GGUF-readability validation both passed ('ok':true, real installed path under ~/.local/share/membrane/models/). checksum_verified came back false: sha256sum (GNU coreutils) is not preinstalled on this runner -- download_manager.cpp's own pre-existing, already-disclosed TOOL_UNAVAILABLE degradation path (PR D1), not a new bug -- confirmed by reading download_manager.cpp's own real source, not assumed.

Real generation: `membrane-run --model ... --ctx 2048 --auto --gpu-layers auto` (adaptive KV, via --auto) succeeded genuinely: 'ok':true, 'execution':{'success':true,'exit_code':0,'generated_tokens':128}.
'gpu':{'backend':'MTL','device_selected':'MTL0','gpu_layers_selected':30} -- full 30/30-layer GPU residency, same full-residency outcome PR D3's CUDA run achieved.
Adaptive KV selected q8 ('adaptive_reason':'Q8_FULL_RESIDENCY'), matching the joint planner's own real, unmodified selection logic.
Real driver-reported GPU memory delta: device_free_bytes_before=5010800640, device_free_bytes_after=4906663936, observed_delta_bytes=104136704.

planner.used=true, policy_version='joint-auto-v1', fallback.attempted=false (the primary candidate succeeded immediately) -- confirms the planner treats Metal exactly like every other backend, no special-casing required, same as PR D3's own finding.

Throughput was very low: decode_tokens_per_second=0.413230 (~310 real seconds for 128 tokens) -- disclosed honestly, not hidden. This is treated as evidence of the paravirtualized GPU's own overhead (the identical model/quant/adaptive-KV combination measured 175 decode tok/s on real bare-metal CUDA hardware in PR D3), not a MEMBRANE inefficiency -- but no strong causal claim is made without a bare-metal Mac to compare against; see docs/macos-metal.md's 'Hardware scope'.

A real, first-attempt finding at this same step: --ctx auto (the fully-automatic form) failed closed with PLANNER_REJECTED_ALL, because host_memory_guard.h's host-RAM read is Linux-only and there is no host-memory fact to size against on macOS -- this is the project's own existing, deliberate 'never proceed on unknown host memory' safety policy working exactly as designed, not a bug. An explicit --ctx N (the CLI's own documented example 5 for this exact situation) was used instead to obtain the real generation evidence above.
Only the --kv adaptive (-> q8) default path was exercised for real this phase; --kv q5/native and --kv-placement cpu were not separately tested on Metal -- see docs/compatibility.json's MC-32 row.

service_lifecycle_smoke.label: REAL
evidence: Real launchd LaunchAgent install/start/status/stop/uninstall cycle against a real per-session launchd (gui/<uid>) on the CI runner -- this CI step's own continue-on-error fallback was never actually needed (the full sequence succeeded genuinely).
`membrane service install`: real plist written to /Users/runner/Library/LaunchAgents/com.membrane.server.plist.
`membrane service start`: real `launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid> <plist>` succeeded (printed 'start').

`membrane service status`: real `launchctl print gui/<uid>/com.membrane.server` parsed successfully -- 'state: running (unknown)' (sub_state stays 'unknown' by design on macOS, launchd has no systemd-style SubState concept), a real pid (21558 in the final run), 'http: not reachable' (expected -- the installed binary here is the `membrane` control CLI itself passed via --exec-path, not a real model-serving `membrane serve` invocation, so no HTTP server was actually listening; this smoke validates the launchd lifecycle mechanism, not end-to-end serving).
`membrane service stop`: real `launchctl bootout` succeeded.
`membrane service uninstall`: real plist file removed, confirmed by a subsequent 'Uninstalled ...' message and no leftover file.

known_limitations.label: SOURCE_ANALYSIS
items: `--ctx auto` does not work on macOS yet -- host_memory_guard.h's real host-RAM reader is Linux-only (/proc/meminfo); extending it to read real memory on macOS (e.g. sysctl hw.memsize) is real, disclosed future work, out of this PR's own scope.

Checksum verification (sha256) does not run on a stock macOS install -- sha256sum (GNU coreutils) is not preinstalled; download_manager.cpp's own pre-existing TOOL_UNAVAILABLE degradation handles this gracefully (real size+GGUF validation still occurs), but real checksum verification requires `brew install coreutils` separately.

`membrane doctor`'s service-status check (tools/membrane/doctor_cmd.cpp) remains systemd/systemctl-specific -- distinct from the cross-platform, real-tested `membrane-run --doctor`. Not exercised by this PR's own CI job; membrane_run_subprocess()'s existing exec-failure handling reports a graceful (if systemd-flavored) message rather than crashing, confirmed by source reading, not a live macOS run.
One real device tested this phase (a paravirtualized MTL0, GitHub's macos-14 runner) -- not a claim about any other Mac, Apple Silicon generation, or real bare-metal Apple GPU performance.
No official macOS package (.pkg/Homebrew formula/etc.) exists yet -- source build only, matching PR D3's own CUDA packaging decision.
--kv q5/native and --kv-placement cpu were not separately exercised on Metal this phase -- only the --kv adaptive (-> q8) default path was real-tested.
